extracted.intended_audience: authors, researchers, trialists, journal editors and peer reviewers involved in randomized trials (protocol and results reporting)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and reporting randomized trial protocols and trial results so they are complete, transparent, and usable for critical appraisal, interpretation, and application. Covers SPIRIT (protocol) and CONSORT (results) checklists, figures/flow diagrams, and supporting explanation documents and tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPIRIT Statement (2025) — 34‑item checklist for trial protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: The SPIRIT (Standard Protocol Items: Recommendations for Interventional Trials) Statement is a minimum set of recommendations for reporting the protocol of a randomised trial. The recommendations are outlined in a 34-item checklist and a figure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the SPIRIT checklist and figure to ensure trial protocols include all recommended items; consult the SPIRIT 'Explanation and Elaboration' document which explains and illustrates the principles underlying the Statement. The aim is to report protocols completely and transparently so readers can appraise, interpret, and use the research.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT Statement (2025) — 30‑item checklist for trial results
rubrics_metrics.description: The CONSORT (CONsolidated Standards Of Reporting Trials) Statement is an evidence-based, minimum set of recommendations for reporting the results of randomised trials. The recommendations are outlined in a 30-item checklist and a flow diagram.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the CONSORT checklist to report how the trial was designed, analysed, and interpreted; include the CONSORT flow diagram which displays the progress of all participants through the trial. Consult the CONSORT 'Explanation and Elaboration' document for detailed examples and rationale. These are minimum, evidence-based recommendations to promote transparent, complete reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete and transparent reporting to enable critical appraisal
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports (protocols and results) should be complete and transparent, providing readers with all the information they need to critically appraise, interpret and use the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This overarching desideratum underpins SPIRIT and CONSORT: use the checklists and Explanation & Elaboration documents to achieve completeness and transparency. Reporting should cover design, analysis, interpretation, and participant flow so that reviewers and readers can assess validity and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of recommended electronic tools (SEPTRE, COBWEB) to prepare and manage documents
rubrics_metrics.description: SEPTRE is an online tool to create, register, and manage trial protocols. COBWEB is an online writing aid to help write, edit, share and export a randomised trial report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SEPTRE for protocol creation/registration and COBWEB as a writing/editing aid to help implement SPIRIT and CONSORT items in practical document workflows. These tools are recommended resources to support adherence to the reporting guidelines.
